newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem raises Argentine growth projection to 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Menem raises Argentine growth projection to 6 pct.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said Monday the economy will grow this year "at least six percent" against a previous official projection of five percent for 1997, and compared with an estimated growth rate of four percent in 1996.

During an official visit to Vietnam, he added the fiscal deficit will not exceed the $3.0 billion agreed with the International Monetary Fund for 1997, according to a transcript of his comments released by the presidency.

"The minister of Economy (Roque Fernandez) is being conservative about it, as he talks about a five percent (growth for 1997), which is the number we included in the budget, but I myself am calculating a six percent growth," Menem said.
He added that although the deficit grew to $6.0 billion last year, "now it is declining steadily."
"We think that for this year it will not exceed half of those $6.0 billion," Menem said.

A letter of intent signed with the IMF envisages a $3.0 billion fiscal deficit that grows to $4.5 billion when including the cost of the transfer of the national pension system to provincial jurisdiction.
